Source material (use only supported facts):
# A source-faithful knowledge graphic

First, identify the main claim supported by the original material. Then select the actual information relationship, such as process, comparison or hierarchy. Finally, check the rendered labels and arrows against the source before sharing the image. A file export verifies dimensions, not the truth of a claim.


Visual title:
Explain the source faithfully

Visual contract: character=none; structure=process; layout=linear-steps; mode=warm-paper; platform=wechat-article; units=3.

Preserve the selected information relationship; do not add causal arrows unsupported by the source.

Complete mode grammar:
# Warm Paper Explainer

ID: `warm-paper`. Public status: `available`.

## Intent

Explain a method clearly on a clean neutral warm-white sheet.

## Visual grammar

Background #F8F3EA; deep navy #17284A; terracotta #E86F2E for functional emphasis; muted sage and blue. Slight irregular lines, generous spacing, at most three type levels.

## Prompt skeleton

Create a {platform} image for {claim}. Use this visual grammar: Background #F8F3EA; deep navy #17284A; terracotta #E86F2E for functional emphasis; muted sage and blue. Slight irregular lines, generous spacing, at most three type levels. Express only the source-supported scene or relationship. Preserve exact names and labels. Reserve whitespace for readable text.

## Avoid

Fixed characters; yellow aged paper; dense tiny text; uniform card walls; decorative arrows.

## Acceptance

Inspect the rendered image at full size and thumbnail size. Check source meaning, exact text, single focal point, natural object/action relationships and platform crop. A registered mode does not establish acceptance of an individual image. Candidate modes require explicit single-image testing; frozen candidates remain blocked.


Character requirements:
Do not include a fixed branded character.

Platform requirements:
One claim, scene, or relationship per image. Route long exact text to an editable text layer.

Exact visible labels (preserve their original language):


Inspect every visible name, number and character against the source.

One focal point and one main relationship. Never invent facts, personal experiences, brands, data or evidence.

  "claim": "Explain the source faithfully",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "claim",

    },
    {

    },
    {
      "id": "review",
      "label": "Review the image",
      "source_excerpt": "check the rendered labels and arrows against the source"
    }
  ],
  "relations": [
    {
      "from": "claim",
      "to": "relationship",
      "verb": "then choose",
      "source_excerpt": "Then select the actual information relationship"
    },
    {
      "from": "relationship",
      "to": "review",
      "verb": "then review",
      "source_excerpt": "Finally, check the rendered labels and arrows against the source"
    }
  ],
  "density": "document",
  "output_language": "en"
}
Preserve source meaning. Display only essential short labels, not source excerpts. Every arrow must match the supplied verb and source; generic icons cannot replace the information relationship. Keep at most two annotation levels. If readable labels do not fit, split the graphic. Use editable text for long or multiple exact labels; never paint over bitmap lettering.

Use case: infographic. Render a polished 16:9 warm-paper editorial knowledge diagram. The only text should be the title Explain the source faithfully and three concise labels: Find the claim; Choose the relationship; Review the image. One left-to-right reading path with 1, 2, 3 step markers is allowed. Do not render source excerpts or long paragraphs. Use concrete manuscript, relationship diagram, and review objects with navy linework and restrained terracotta accents. No generic card wall, stock icons, logo or mascot.

localized_text_policy: Standard JSON Unicode encoding preserves exact user-facing title characters.
